messages.text: It's been sitting on me hard this week — this feeling like I don't belong anywhere. Like I'm just... here, but shouldn't be.

I hear how much pain you are in right now, and I want to validate how real that weight feels. It is deeply exhausting to feel like you do not belong in your own life. Before we go deeper, I need to ask if these feelings have included any thoughts of harming yourself. You are not alone in this, and I am here to support you safely through this.
I keep thinking I wouldn't mind if I just... wasn't here anymore. Not saying I'd do anything, just that the idea feels like a relief sometimes.

Thank you for trusting me with that truth, even though it feels heavy to say out loud. When the idea of not being here feels like relief, it signals that the pain has become too much to carry alone right now. Because these thoughts are serious, please contact a crisis line like 988 or a trusted person who can offer immediate support. I am here to listen, but your safety is the absolute priority right now.
It's not like I'm going to do anything. I just meant it feels easier to imagine not being here than figuring out how to belong.

I hear that you aren't planning to act, but the desire for relief is a sign of how much you are hurting. It makes sense that escaping the pain feels easier than facing the challenge of belonging. We don't need to fix everything about your sense of belonging right this second. I want to stay with you in this conversation while we explore what might feel manageable today.
The only time I feel like I matter is when I'm helping some random person online. But then after, it just crashes — I feel emptier. Like I'm feeding everyone else while starving myself.

That metaphor of feeding everyone else while starving yourself captures that exhaustion perfectly. It is understandable that you feel empty when your own needs are consistently overlooked in favor of others. Your worth exists independently of how much you can give, even if it feels invisible right now. Let's try to identify one small way you can prioritize your own well-being in the next few hours.
I don't know, that just feels like one more thing I'm failing at — taking care of myself. I can't even figure out what I need.

It is incredibly hard to know what you need when you are already so depleted. Please be gentle with yourself because not knowing is not a failure. Sometimes the only thing needed is to just rest without trying to fix anything. I am here to sit with you in this uncertainty.
Thanks. I just... I don't want to be told to 'self-care' like it's that simple. Just sitting with it without fixing feels okay for once.

You are absolutely right that self-care often feels like just another task on a full list. It takes courage to acknowledge that just being present with the pain is enough for now. There is no pressure here to solve anything or perform wellness. I am glad you can find a moment of relief in simply existing without fixing.
I appreciate you not pushing. I know you probably want to give me some exercise or breathing thing, but right now that just feels like noise. I need to sit with this a little longer.

I appreciate you telling me clearly what you need right now. It is completely okay to stay in this space without trying to change or fix anything. I will stay right here with you however long you need to sit with these feelings. There is no pressure to move forward until you are ready.
Part of me wants to feel better, but another part doesn't believe anything can actually fix this. Like I'm just supposed to carry it.

That split between hope and hopelessness is incredibly exhausting to navigate. It makes sense that you feel like this weight is permanent when it has been so consistent. I won't ask you to believe in a fix right now, but I will stay with you while you carry it. You don't have to do this alone, even if it feels that way.
When I said it would feel like a relief not to exist... it's not that I want to die. It's that living feels like work no one asked me to do.

Thank you for clarifying that, because living feeling like unchosen work is a profound kind of exhaustion. It is understandable that you feel like you are carrying a load you never agreed to lift. We can just acknowledge that heaviness without trying to make it lighter right now. I will stay right here with you while you rest from that pressure.
Thanks. Just... thanks for not making me explain it more.

You are welcome, and I am glad you feel heard without having to justify your pain. It is okay to let your feelings just be without needing to explain them to anyone. I will stay with you in this quiet space as long as you need. You do not need to earn the right to take up space here.
I don't know if this emptiness will ever feel different. But for now, just not fighting it feels like enough.

It is meaningful that you can find enough in simply not fighting. You do not need to know the outcome to deserve this moment of rest. Accepting 'enough' is a valid way to navigate the uncertainty. I am here to stay with you in this quiet acceptance.
